topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the scope of the cancer lecture series, and presents the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetics, Bad Luck, and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the core principles of cancer development, debating the relative contributions of intrinsic random mutations, inherited genetics, and environmental exposures supported by global epidemiological data.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the specific biological, chemical, and physical mechanisms by which diverse agents directly cause DNA damage or indirectly promote tumor progression.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying Carcinogens and Mutational Signatures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental methodologies used to detect carcinogenicity and trace mutational patterns.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic concludes the lecture by summarising the challenges of determining carcinogen potency and reflecting on daily risk-benefit decisions.
